title: Medical Genetics - Year 1 Fundamentals
description: Introductory medical genetics covering inheritance patterns, chromosomal disorders, molecular genetics, and genetic diseases for Year 1 medical students.

questions.question_text: What is the normal human chromosome number?
questions.explanation: Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs): 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.question_text: What is Down syndrome caused by?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome is caused by trisomy 21 - having three copies of chromosome 21 instead of two.

questions.question_text: What inheritance pattern is shown when both parents must be carriers for a child to be affected?
questions.explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance requires two copies of the mutant allele (one from each carrier parent).
A karyotype is an organized image of chromosomes arranged by size and shape, used to detect abnormalities.

answers.answer_text: An organized display of chromosomes from a cell

questions.question_text: Sickle cell disease is an example of which type of inheritance?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell disease is autosomal recessive - you need two copies of the mutant HBB gene to be affected.
A point mutation is a change in a single nucleotide base in the DNA sequence.

answers.answer_text: A change in a single nucleotide base

questions.question_text: What is Huntington's disease inheritance pattern?
questions.explanation: Huntington's disease is autosomal dominant - only one copy of the mutant gene causes the disease.

questions.question_text: What is the sex chromosome constitution of a male?
questions.explanation: Males have XY sex chromosomes; females have XX.
Turner syndrome is caused by monosomy X (45,X) - having only one X chromosome in females.

questions.question_text: What is a carrier in genetics?
questions.explanation: A carrier has one copy of a recessive disease allele but doesn't show symptoms (heterozygous).

answers.answer_text: A person with one copy of a recessive allele who doesn't show symptoms
A person affected by a genetic disease
A person with two dominant alleles
A person without any genetic mutations

questions.question_text: Hemophilia A is an example of which inheritance pattern?
questions.explanation: Hemophilia A is X-linked recessive - the gene is on the X chromosome, so males are more commonly affected.
A frameshift mutation occurs when insertions or deletions (not multiples of 3) shift the reading frame.

answers.answer_text: An insertion or deletion that shifts the reading frame
A substitution of one base for another
A mutation that has no effect

questions.explanation: Klinefelter syndrome is 47,XXY - males with an extra X chromosome, causing infertility and other features.

answers.answer_text: A condition where males have an extra X chromosome (47,XXY)
A condition where females have an extra X chromosome
A condition with only one X chromosome

questions.question_text: What is a pedigree chart used for?
questions.explanation: A pedigree chart shows inheritance patterns of traits/diseases across multiple generations of a family.

answers.answer_text: To track inheritance patterns in a family

questions.explanation: Mitochondrial DNA is inherited only from the mother (maternal inheritance) because sperm mitochondria are destroyed.
Penetrance is the proportion of individuals with a mutation who actually express the phenotype.

answers.answer_text: The proportion of people with a mutation who show the phenotype
How severe a genetic disease is

questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, most commonly the ΔF508 deletion.
A nonsense mutation creates a premature stop codon, resulting in a truncated (shortened) protein.

answers.answer_text: A mutation that creates a premature stop codon
A mutation that changes one amino acid to another
A silent mutation with no effect
A mutation that adds extra codons

questions.explanation: Edwards syndrome is trisomy 18 - three copies of chromosome 18, causing severe developmental abnormalities.
Expressivity refers to the degree or severity of phenotype expression in individuals with the same genotype.

answers.answer_text: The degree of phenotype variation among individuals with the same genotype
Whether a gene is expressed at all

questions.explanation: A translocation is when part of one chromosome breaks off and attaches to another chromosome.

answers.answer_text: When parts of chromosomes break off and attach to different chromosomes

questions.explanation: Patau syndrome is trisomy 13, causing severe intellectual disability and physical abnormalities.
Anticipation is when a genetic disorder appears earlier or more severe in successive generations (e.g., trinucleotide repeat disorders).

answers.answer_text: Disease appearing earlier or more severe in successive generations

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of amniocentesis?
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis samples amniotic fluid to test fetal cells for chromosomal abnormalities and genetic disorders.

answers.answer_text: To test fetal cells for chromosomal abnormalities
To determine the mother's blood type

questions.question_text: What percentage of children are affected when both parents are carriers of an autosomal recessive condition?
questions.explanation: If both parents are carriers (Aa × Aa), 25% of children will be affected (aa), 50% carriers, 25% unaffected.
